Recipe:
Stealth-Attack Chili 10-12 servings A VanOrman Original
§ion; &parentSection;
This is one of the first recipes invented by Ransom. He wanted a good recipe that could be made with ingredients primarily from food storage. We went through several attempts, but once we succeeded, we would make it over and over. Due to the spices, it takes 4-5 bites before you realized it is very spicy hot. (Thus stealth-attack.)
Unfortunately, when we moved to Washington, nobody could stand how hot it was. (It's not that hot to me.) And when made for Boy Scout competitions, it didn't have a good "look" to it, so we invented Entrees / Stove Top: Klondike Chili. But, we still make this one from time to time.
Dried Kidney Beans2 Cups Dried Red Beans1 Cup Dried Pinto Beans1 Cup Water2 Quarts Hamburger1 Lb. Dried Minced Onion½-1 Cup Chili Powder1-2 Tablespoons Cayenne Pepper½-2 teaspoons Black Pepper½-2 teaspoons Garlic Powder1 teaspoon
Celery Seed2 teaspoons Paprika½ teaspoon Cumin2 teaspoons Salt2 Tablespoons Brown Sugar2 Tablespoons Tomato Sauce3 8-oz. Cans Tomato Paste2 6-oz. Cans Tomatoes6 Water½-2 Cups
Put Water and beans in a Slow Cooker and cook them on Low overnight. (4-8 hours) Drain all of the excess Water, leaving beans in the Slow Cooker. Brown Hamburger, until there is no pink meat left, then add to the Slow Cooker. Put all other ingredients into the Slow Cooker, except Water, and mix well. Add Water until Chili is at desired consistency. Cook on High for 2-4 hours or Low for 4-8 hours.
Dried beans are hard. They need to be softened before they can be eaten. That is why you have to start the recipe the night before.
People have different tastes for spiciness. Use the minimum if you like Mild. The max if you like Hot, or somewhere in between for a Medium.
May substitute 2 Onions cut into ¼&inch; disks, then disks cut into 4 wedges for Dried Minced Onion. May substitute 1 teaspoon Minced Garlic for the Garlic Powder. May substitute 2 Tablespoons Light Corn Syrup for the Brown Sugar. May substitute 2 14.5-oz. cans Diced Tomatoes for the Tomatoes. This can be cooked on the stove in a large pot by substituting 3-4 cans of beans for the dried beans, then simmer on medium low for 15-30 minutes.
